nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of variables and a CNF clause $C$, this Boolean test is true exactly when every negative literal of $C$ has its variable in $T$.
nodes.title: Body of a clause contained in a set

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the closure of $T$ is computed by iterating the forward-chaining step of $\varphi$: if every variable derived from $T$ already lies in $T$, the closure is $T$; otherwise it is the closure of the union of $T$ with the derived variables.
nodes.title: Forward-chaining closure

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the derived set consists of the variables $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains the positive literal $x$ and has every one of its negative literals on a variable in $T$.
nodes.title: Forward-chaining step

nodes.summary: If $\varphi$ is a Horn CNF formula, then the Horn satisfiability test returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Horn satisfiability test

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the Horn satisfiability test returns the Boolean truth value of $\varphi$ under its least model candidate.
nodes.title: Horn satisfiability test

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a Horn formula when every clause contains at most one distinct positive literal.
nodes.title: Horn formula

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a Horn CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment satisfying $\varphi$. Every variable that the least model candidate of $\varphi$ makes true is also true under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: On Horn formulas, the least model candidate lies below every model

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the least model candidate is the assignment that makes a variable true exactly when it lies in the forward-chaining closure of the empty set under $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Least model candidate

nodes.summary: A Horn CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if its least model candidate satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Horn satisfiability via the least model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
